CITY OF SIGNAL HILL

  THE CITY OF SIGNAL HILL

  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  October 10, 2023

  REVISED

Meetings begin at 6:00 pm with the conduct of any business permitted to be conducted in
closed session by the Brown Act (Government Code Section 54950, et seq.), if any, and with
the public portion of the meeting beginning at 7:00 pm. There is a period for public comment
on closed session matters at 6:00 pm prior to the closed session. In the event there is no
business to be conducted in closed session, the regular meeting shall begin at 7:00 pm.
There is a public comment period at the beginning of the regular meeting. Any person
wishing to comment shall be allotted three minutes per distinct item. Any meeting may be
adjourned to a time and place stated in the order of adjournment.

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting on the City’s website and outside of City
Hall. The agenda and related reports are also available for review online at
www.cityofsignalhill.org.

To view or listen to the meeting live at 7:00 p.m.:

  • City of Signal Hill website at www.cityofsignalhill.org, select the City Council
  Meetings Link from the home page.
  • Charter Spectrum Channel 3 or Frontier FiOS Channel 38.
To participate (closed session at 6:00 p.m. and regular meeting at 7:00 p.m.):

  • In-person Participation: Council Chambers of City Hall, 2175 Cherry Avenue, Signal
  Hill, California.
  • To make a general public comment or comment on a specific agenda item, you may
  also submit your comment, limited to 250 words or less, to the City Clerk at
  cityclerk@cityofsignalhill.org not later than 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, October 10, 2023.
  Written comments will be provided electronically to City Council and attached to the
  meeting minutes. Written comments will not be read into the record.
City Council Members are compensated $722.18 per month. City Clerk and City Treasurer are
compensated $438.22 per month.

  a.  SELECTION OF NATIONAL COMMUNITY RENAISSANCE AS THE CITY’S
  DEVELOPMENT PARTNER FOR THE ORANGE BLUFF AND WALNUT BLUFF
  WORKFORCE HOUSING SITES

  Summary:

  In April, the City Council and Housing Authority Board authorized staff to issue a
  Notice of Funding Availability (NOFA) totaling approximately $10 million to
  leverage toward the development of the Orange Bluff and Walnut Bluff
  workforce housing sites. Staff received six proposals; after conducting an
  extensive selection process, including in-person interviews and onsite property
  tours, staff recommends National Community Renaissance (National CORE) as
  the preferred development partner. As one of the largest nonprofit developers in
  the United States, National CORE has a strong reputation for developing
  high-quality properties. Among the distinguishing features of National CORE’s
  proposal was its comprehensive redevelopment plan to fund the cost of
  infrastructure improvements, not only for the workforce housing sites, but also
  for the Heritage Square and Town Center Northwest sites. National CORE also
  proposed a robust social services component, including the development of a
  5,000 square foot Boys and Girls Club. Staff recommends the City Council and
  Housing Authority Board select National CORE and direct staff to negotiate an
  Exclusive Negotiation Agreement to effectuate the next steps in the
  development process. Over the next few months, staff would negotiate the
  terms of the ENA and return to the City Council and Housing Authority Board
  with the final recommended document for approval.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s)

  Goal No. 1  Financial Stability: Ensure the City’s long-term financial stability
  and resilience.

  Goal No. 3  Economic Development: Improve the local economy, support local
  businesses, and create a vibrant downtown core.

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s  physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends the City Council and Housing Authority Board select National
  Community Renaissance as the City’s development partner and direct staff to
  negotiate an Exclusive Negotiation Agreement (ENA) for the development of the
  Orange Bluff and Walnut Bluff workforce housing sites.

RECESS THE HOUSING AUTHORITY

  b.  CONTRACT SERVICES AGREEMENTS WITH W.A. RASIC CONSTRUCTION
  COMPANY, INCORPORATED AND T.E. ROBERTS, INCORPORATED FOR
  ON-CALL WATER INFRASTRUCTURE MAINTENANCE AND REPAIR
  SERVICES

  Summary:

  The City Council will consider entering into Contract Services Agreements with
  W.A. Rasic Construction Company, Incorporated and T.E. Roberts, Incorporated
  for on-call water infrastructure maintenance and repair services. The proposed
  contracts would serve on an as-needed basis to provide emergency and
  non-emergency services to the City’s water system.

  Strategic Goal(s):

  Goal No. 4  Infrastructure: Maintain and improve the City’s  physical
  infrastructure, water system, and recreational spaces.
  Recommendations:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to award a Contract Services Agreement to W .A.
  Rasic Construction Company, Incorporated for as-needed water
  maintenance and repair services, for a not-to-exceed amount of $200,000 in
  a form approved by the City Attorney. The term of this agreement is for
  one-year with no more than three additional one-year extensions.

  2. Authorize the City Manager to award a Contract Services Agreement to T.E.
  Roberts, Incorporated for as-needed water maintenance and repair services,
  for a not-to-exceed amount of $200,000 in a form approved by the City
  Attorney. The term of this agreement is for one-year with no more than three
  additional one-year extensions.

  a.  FEE  WAIVER  REQUEST  FOR  THE  SUSTAINABLE  HEALTH
  EMPOWERMENT (SHE) HEALTH FAIR ON SATURDAY, NOVEMBER 4, 2023

  Summary:

  Staff received a request from the Office of Sustainable Health Empowerment
  (SHE), a local Long Beach non-profit organization, for a fee waiver for the use of
  the Signal Point Terrace; Library Community Room; Library Learning Center;
  Zinnia Courtyard; Signal Hill Park Picnic Shelter #3, and Signal Hill Park Open
  Grass Area; and City staff fees associated with facilitation and coverage for the
  Page 4 of 6

  Community Equity Health Fair on Saturday, November 4, 2023, from 8:00 a.m.
  to 4:00 p.m., and fees to stage the area on Friday, November 3, 2023.

  Strategic Plan Goal(s):

  Goal No. 2  Community Safety: Maintain community safety by supporting
  public safety services and increasing emergency preparedness.

  Goal No. 5  High-Functioning Government: Strengthen internal communication,
  recruitment, retention, systems, and processes to increase the
  effectiveness and efficiency of City services.
  Recommendation:

  Staff recommends the City Council review and approve a waiver of fees for use
  of the Signal Point Terrace; Library Community Room; Library Learning Center;
  Zinnia Courtyard; Signal Hill Park Picnic Shelter #3; and Signal Hill Open Grass
  Area; and City staff costs associated with the facilitation of the rental, including
  staging on Friday, November 3, 2023.

  b.  WARRANT REGISTER DATED OCTOBER 10, 2023

  Summary:

  The Warrant Register is a listing of all general disbursements issued since the

CITIZEN PARTICIPATION

  Routine matters are handled most quickly and efficiently if contact is made with the City
  department directly concerned. However, if you would like to request that a matter be
  presented for City Council consideration, you may do so by writing to the City Council,
  City Clerk, or City Manager. The deadline for agenda items is 12 noon on the Tuesday
  preceding the Council and Agency meetings. The complete agenda, including back up
  materials is available on the City website on the Friday preceding the meeting.

  If you need special assistance beyond what is normally provided to participate in City
  meetings, the City will attempt to accommodate you in every reasonable manner.
  Please call the City Clerk's office at (562) 989-7305 at least 48 hours prior to the
  meeting to inform us of your particular needs and to determine if accommodation is
  feasible.
